nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Partnerships for the goals|Global sustainability regulation|Climate change agreements_qna_000
nodes.question: What are the key features of the Rotterdam Climate Agreement?
nodes.answer: The Rotterdam Climate Agreement focuses on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving air quality, and increasing sustainable energy use in the city to combat climate change.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Partnerships for the goals|Global sustainability regulation|Climate change agreements_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What role do international agreements play in addressing climate change?
nodes.answer: International agreements influence long-term strategic policies of each country and are fundamental tools for promoting policies that tackle immediate needs sustainably and contribute to a safer future.
nodes.paragraph: International agreements offer a platform for integrating national policies into a global framework. Climate change require long-term strategic policy of each country that can be influenced by the obligations undertaken in international agreements. International agreements provide a frame- work for managing conflicts and tensions between countries and promoting policies that not only address immediate needs but are also sustainable and oriented toward a safer future. Agreements, through cooperation among countries, are fundamen- tal tools to ensure that national policies align with global sustainability, inequality reduction, and resilience goals. Studying these dynamics helps to better understand how international negotiations work, the implementation mechanisms, and the impacts of climate policies on a global scale. During the past three decades, IEAs have been proposed as the only possible solution to control global warming, caused by consumption and production activities among all countries. It is common knowl- edge that cooperation in IEAs is quite difficult to reach because each country would prefer to participate in an agreement in order to reduce pollution and preserve the environment but, at the same time, it would pursue its self interest.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Partnerships for the goals|Global sustainability regulation|Climate change agreements_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What type of literature has emerged regarding International Environmental Agreements (IEAs)?
nodes.answer: Recent literature has focused on the combination of mitigation and adaptation measures within IEAs as tools to combat climate change.
nodes.paragraph: Most countries facing a transboundary pollution problem implement one of two political strategies: mitigation and adaptation. Mitigation policies aimed at reducing carbon emissions instead adaptation measures meant to reduce pollution damage, considering the dramatic effects of the accumulation and increase in the concen- tration of pollutant which persists in the atmosphere for decades. While mitigation consists of any means aimed at curtailing the pollution emission of countries, adap- tation is increasingly considered a policy response to climate change alongside the Stability of International Environmental Agreements: Effects mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions, its measures consist of a set of actions that prevent or decrease the adverse effects of accumulated pollution. The literature look - ing at IEAs combining mitigation and adaptation measures is quite recent. Benchek - roun et al. (2017), Borrero and Rubio (2022), Breton and Sbragia (2019), Lazkano et al. (2016), Masoudi and Zaccour (2017), Rohrer and Rubio (2024) and Masoudi and Zaccour (2018) focus on the strategic role of mitigation and adaptation in the IEAs as a tool to combat climate change.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Partnerships for the goals|Global sustainability regulation|Climate change agreements_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How do Bayramoglu et al. (2018) contribute to the understanding of adaptation and mitigation in climate agreements?
nodes.answer: They study the strategic interaction between mitigation, viewed as a public good, and adaptation, considered a private good in the context of a climate agreement.
nodes.paragraph: While mitigation activity is always consid- ered as a public, international good, about adaptation, different scenarios have been proposed. In Lazkano et al. (2016), Rohrer and Rubio (2024) and Benchekroun et al. (2017) adaptation is a private good that only affects the welfare of the host coun- try instead (Masoudi & Zaccour 2017) and Masoudi and Zaccour (2018) assume that adaptation has a public good flavor. In Bayramoglu et al. (2018) it is studied the strategic interaction between mitigation (public good) and adaptation (private good) in a climate agreement. The view that adaptation is a private good is certainly correct when the focus is on the use of a specific adaptation technology. However, new knowledge about adaptation requires investments in research and development (R&D), which can be shared by different entities, with the resulting new technolo- gies benefiting all parties. All paper cited are modelled as a multi-stage game where players select their level of emissions and their level of adaptation in different stages and results indicate that the simultaneous deciding of adaptation and mitigation levels may have a positive effect on the stability of IEAs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Governance|Partnerships for the goals|Global sustainability regulation|Climate change agreements_qna_012
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the names of some major international climate agreements mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The Kyoto Protocol and COP21 are major international climate agreements mentioned in the paragraph.
nodes.paragraph: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change7 has highlighted that activities such as desertification, deforestation, and global warming have environmental implications. Carbon dioxide (CO2) represents the most significant portion of GHGs, making it a primary environmental pollutant of concern6,8,9. Economic growth driven by trade openness and industrialisation can exacerbate environmental pollution and contribute to climate change through increased industrial activities and consumption1 11. 1Institute of Climate and Environment, SIMAD University, Mogadishu, Somalia. 2Faculty of Economics, SIMAD University, Mogadishu, Somalia. 3Faculty of Management Sciences, SIMAD University, Mogadishu, Somalia. email: abdikafihasan79@gmail.com OPEN Scientific Reports www.nature.com/scientificreports Environmental scientists, researchers, and policymakers have convened to deploy cutting-edge mitigation strategies in response to grave concerns posed by the ongoing rise in global temperatures12. The Kyoto Protocol and COP21 are major international climate agreements that address environmental challenges, with participating nations committed to reducing CO2 emissions to diminish global temperature by 2 C13. Several factors influence environmental quality, including globalisation, trade openness, economic growth, and renewable energy. Although energy generation and use are essential for economic growth, they present challenges, including environmental pollution, which impede ecological sustainability14.
